correctness.rationale: The row-column identity |N(i,j) intersect S|=r_i+c_j-2x_ij is exact. When both dimensions are at least three, the two-small-degrees obstruction proves that all feasible sets must be single full rows or columns of length three. For two rows, column types are exhaustively divided into only doubles, a double-plus-singleton, or a full row of length two or three, giving the stated polynomial with correct boundary indicators. All constructed types directly satisfy the defining constraints. Two distinct executable procedures checked 13 and 19 finite boards; they corroborate, not replace, the all-order proof. Risks: no formal proof assistant or independent mathematical referee has verified the text.

originality.rationale: The statement is a complete labelled all-set polynomial and a sharp iff existence threshold for two-factor rook graphs. The 2013 founding article studies non-total [1,2]-sets on K_p Cartesian K_2 and poses the total variant; the 2015 foundational total paper provides broad bounds and sufficient absence conditions; 2017 toroidal-cycle work entails only the numeric 3-by-3 minimum special case; a later total-k product paper has no two-neighbor ceiling. Actual scientific record searches in multiple equivalent formulations found no stronger formula implying the present classification. The 2013 publisher full text was not completely accessible and priority is not independently settled.
residual_risks: The full 2013 publisher version could not be retrieved; only indexed relevant article material was available.

value.rationale: The founding total-[1,2] question explicitly motivates which graphs support locally one-or-two coverage. The exact two-parameter cutoff at min(m,n)=3 exhibits an obstruction for every larger rook grid despite the existence of ordinary total dominating sets; the complete polynomial counts all feasible configurations and explains the exceptional small boards rather than merely furnishing a minimum number. This is a natural complete family classification, not a preselected arbitrary instance; the limits are stated.
